proposed.why: The evidence ties the 100x over-charges to the payments-api deploy at 07:20:55; the settings and timing are enough to propose a rollback.

diagnosis.hypothesis: The payments-api deploy at 07:20:55 set CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. The service now sends the provider an amount 100x too large, probably treating a cents value as dollars and converting it again. Our own records keep the correct amount (e.g. pmt_000242 = 1882 cents), but the provider charges 188200. This is why payments_match_provider fails on 'amount differs'. The mismatches begin at pmt_000242, which succeeded at 07:20:56, one second after the deploy. The other four invariants pass, so the books, the ledger and the refunds are consistent with the provider; only the payment amounts sent are wrong. The trace does not show the request body, so the 100x factor is inferred from the money check and the deploy timing, not seen in the outgoing call.

evidence.shows: payments_match_provider fails. Every finding is 'amount differs', with the provider's charge exactly 100x ours (1882 vs 188200, 735 vs 73500, and so on), starting at pmt_000242. evidence_total is 66 while the alert and summary say 61; I did not resolve that difference. All other invariants pass.
payments-api was redeployed at 07:20:55 with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. No other service changed after 07:19:29, and none of those changes touched amounts.
pmt_000242 succeeded at 07:20:56 with amount_cents=1882 in our log, just after the deploy.

The trace of pmt_000242 shows a normal flow: insert of the payment, POST to fake-provider returning 200, then update to succeeded. It has no errors and does not show the amount sent, so the cause is a silent wrong value, not a failure.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll payments-api back to the settings it ran before the 07:20:55 deploy, to stop new 100x charges. Then repair the roughly 61-66 payments already over-charged (pmt_000242 onward): the provider's records show the wrong amounts, so refund or correct the difference at the provider and reconcile. The rollback does not repair these. Afterwards, re-run the money check.

diagnosis.blast_radius: payments-api restarts and pauses briefly, so payment and refund requests may fail or time out during the restart. The rollback also reverts PROVIDER_BREAKER and REFUND_CONNECTION to their earlier values, since all three settings changed in the same deploy; I did not see what the earlier values were. Payments already over-charged stay wrong.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the rollback causes problems, redeploy payments-api with its previous settings (PROVIDER_BREAKER=on, REFUND_CONNECTION=returned) and fix CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT separately. Check with the money check and a few new payments that the amounts sent to the provider equal ours.
